key_facts: Gabriel Bortoleto, driving Car 5 for Audi Revolut F1 Team, moved under braking when approaching Turn 5 during the race at the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix on 13 September 2026.
Car 5 impacted Car 43 as a result of this movement, forcing Car 43 off the track.
This breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 e) of the FIA International Sporting Code prohibits drivers from moving under braking in a way that causes contact with another car.
The Stewards issued a Warning to Bortoleto, which is the equivalent to a black/white flag (a warning for unsportsmanlike or dangerous driving).

Gabriel Bortoleto drove Car 5 for Audi Revolut F1 Team in the race at the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix on 13 September 2026. During the race approaching Turn 5, his car moved under braking. This means the car changed position sideways while he was slowing down for the corner. The moving car hit Car 43, which had to leave the track as a result.

The rules say drivers cannot move under braking. This rule exists to stop drivers from using sudden sideways movement to block or push other cars out of the way while braking. The Stewards watched video and in-car camera footage and decided Bortoleto had broken this rule.

The normal penalty for this offence is a black/white flag (a warning for dangerous or unsportsmanlike driving). The Stewards issued a Warning to Bortoleto, which they say is equivalent to a black/white flag.

key_facts: Charles Leclerc, driving car 16 for Scuderia Ferrari HP, left the track and gained a lasting advantage during the race at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix, breaching Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
The Stewards determined that Leclerc's car and another car (car 44) both entered turn 4 with excessive speed and neither could have completed the corner while staying on track.
Leclerc completed an overtake while off track, which the Stewards found warrants a penalty because he was not entitled to claim the corner due to the excessive entry speed.

The Stewards imposed a 5 second time penalty on Leclerc, reduced from the baseline guideline of 10 seconds in mitigation of the fact that car 44 was also off track on the inside and the incident occurred early in the first lap.
summary.plain_explanation:
The Stewards penalised Charles Leclerc, car 16 for Scuderia Ferrari HP, during the race at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix for leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage.

The incident happened at turn 4. Both Leclerc's car and car 44 entered the corner at excessive speed, which meant neither car could stay on track to complete the corner. Car 44, which was on the inside, had to go off track. Leclerc then completed an overtake while his car was off the track.

The Stewards ruled that Leclerc was not allowed to claim the corner because he came in at excessive speed. A driver cannot make a legal overtake if they leave the track to do it. Leclerc breached Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations, which prohibits gaining a lasting advantage by leaving the track.

The Stewards gave Leclerc a 5 second time penalty. The normal starting point for this type of breach is 10 seconds, but the Stewards reduced it because car 44 was also off track on the inside of Leclerc's car, and because the incident happened early in the first lap.

key_facts: Liam Lawson, driving car 30 for Visa Cash App Racing Bulls, breached Articles C5.12.6 and C5.12.7 of the F1 Regulations during Q2 qualifying at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix.

After crossing the control line at the end of his fastest lap, the driver did not lift off the power immediately, which prevented the MGUK (Motor Generator Unit-Kinetic) from reducing its deployment at the required rate.
The team argued the breach gave no performance advantage, but the Stewards found that non-compliance with the Technical Regulations is not excused by lack of performance advantage.
Car 30 is disqualified from the Provisional Qualifying Classifications.
The Stewards noted the team self-disclosed the breach, but precedent requires disqualification for Technical Regulation non-compliance regardless of mitigating circumstances.
summary.plain_explanation:
Liam Lawson and his team Visa Cash App Racing Bulls faced a penalty during Q2 qualifying at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix.

The car did not comply with Articles C5.12.6 and C5.12.7 of the F1 Regulations. Specifically, at the end of his fastest lap in Q2, after crossing the control line, the driver did not lift off the power immediately. This meant the MGUK (Motor Generator Unit-Kinetic, a device that recovers energy during braking) did not reduce its deployment at the rate the regulations require.

The team argued this breach gave the car no performance advantage. However, the Stewards stated that non-compliance with the Technical Regulations cannot be excused simply because no advantage was gained. The regulations require that a car must comply with them at all times during an event.

The Stewards noted that the team themselves reported the problem. Even so, there are many precedents requiring disqualification when a car does not comply with the Technical Regulations, regardless of other circumstances. Car 30 is disqualified from the Provisional Qualifying Classifications.

key_facts: This document sets out instructions for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix held from 30 October to 1 November 2026.
The document covers general race procedures including qualifying session conduct, lapping rules, pit lane operations, practice starts, and track limits.

Drivers must allow faster drivers to overtake when blue light panels are shown (when a faster car is within 1.2 seconds), and drivers exceeding a maximum time between two Safety Car Lines during qualifying or reconnaissance laps may be deemed to be going unnecessarily slowly.
The document specifies that waved yellow flags and SC boards will not be used; instead, messages will be sent to all teams and trackside light panels will display SC when the Safety Car is deployed.
Track limits violations at specific turns (Turn 4, Turn 11, Turn 17) may result in lap time invalidation, rejoin restrictions, or other penalties as determined by the Stewards.
summary.plain_explanation:
This is the Race Director's Competition Notes for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. It sets out how the race will be run at this specific event, on top of the standard rules.

During qualifying and the reconnaissance laps before the race, drivers must not drive too slowly. The Race Director will give teams a maximum time between two points on the track (the Second and First Safety Car Lines). Any driver who exceeds this time on any lap during or after qualifying, or on reconnaissance laps, may be found to be driving unnecessarily slowly. This rule applies to in-laps and out-laps as well as normal laps, and also to the pit lane.

During the race, when a faster driver is catching up to a slower car ahead of them, the marshalling system will first give a warning when the gap is 3 seconds. When the gap closes to 1.2 seconds, blue light panels will be shown to the slower car (along with blue cockpit lights and a message on the timing monitors). The slower driver must then let the faster driver past at the first available opportunity. This rule comes from the International Sporting Code, which requires drivers who are caught and lapped to allow faster drivers through.

The document sets out detailed rules for pit lane operations, practice starts, and parc fermé (the sealed area where cars are kept under official supervision after qualifying and after the race). It explains where cars may and must go during these procedures, and how team personnel may enter restricted areas.

The document also specifies track limits rules for this circuit. At Turn 17, if a driver fails to take the racing line, lap times may be invalidated. At Turn 4, if a driver enters the run-off area and crosses a yellow line with all four wheels, they must rejoin the circuit at a specific point after Turn 5. At Turn 11, if a car goes completely behind the red and white kerb, there are specific rejoin rules using polystyrene blocks.

For Safety Car procedures, this event will not use waved yellow flags or SC boards. Instead, when the Safety Car is deployed, a message "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" will be sent to all teams and all trackside light panels will show SC. When the Safety Car lights are turned off, a message "SAFETY CAR LIGHTS OFF" will be sent, and a green light panel will appear at the Control Line.

Finally, the document lists changes made to the circuit for this race, including a resurfaced section, widened white lines at certain corners, and new positions for the practice start boxes.

summary.plain_explanation:
This document gives competition rules for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. It covers many topics that apply to practice, qualifying, and the race.

One rule is about drivers who are caught and lapped by faster cars during the race. The International Sporting Code requires a driver being lapped to let the faster driver past at the first chance. The marshalling system (the trackside control system) will warn the slower driver's team when the faster car is 3 seconds away, and will show blue light panels to the slower car when the faster car is within 1.2 seconds. At that point, the driver being lapped must allow the faster car to overtake at the first available opportunity.

Another rule is about qualifying and reconnaissance laps. Any driver who takes too long to go from the Second Safety Car Line to the First Safety Car Line on any lap during or after qualifying, including in-laps and out-laps, or during reconnaissance laps when pit exit opens for the race, may be treated as going unnecessarily slowly. The teams and drivers are told the maximum time after the second practice session. This rule does not change the regulations that already apply to the whole circuit and the pit lane.

The document also sets detailed rules about pit lane entry and exit, parc fermé (a closed area where cars are controlled after qualifying or the race), practice starts, and how cars must rejoin the track if they go off at certain corners. For Turn 4, if a driver goes off into the run-off area and crosses a yellow line with all four wheels, they must rejoin via a specific asphalt route. For Turn 11, a driver whose car passes completely behind the red and white kerb must rejoin by keeping to the right of the first polystyrene block and then to the left of the second.

For safety car procedures, the document says that waved yellow flags and "SC" boards will not be used. Instead, when the safety car deploys, the message "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" will be sent to all teams and a trackside light panel will display "SC". When the safety car lights turn off, the message "SAFETY CAR LIGHTS OFF" will be sent to all teams, and a green light panel will show at the Control Line.

The circuit has been resurfaced from after Turn 11 until before Turn 1. Several new blue lines have been added to mark safe routes, and some kerbs and white lines have been changed to make track limits clearer.

summary.plain_explanation:
This document is the Race Director's Competition Notes for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix, issued on 1 November 2026. It contains instructions for teams and officials on how to conduct the event safely and fairly.

During qualifying and reconnaissance laps, drivers must not exceed a maximum time between the Second Safety Car Line and the First Safety Car Line. Teams will be told what this time is after the second practice session. A driver who goes over this time may be penalised for going unnecessarily slowly. This rule applies to all laps during and after qualifying, including in-laps and out-laps, and to reconnaissance laps when the pit exit is opened before the race.

When a faster driver is catching a slower car during the race, the marshalling system will first send a pre-warning message when the faster car is within 3 seconds. When the faster car gets within 1.2 seconds, blue light panels will be shown to the slower car, along with blue cockpit lights and a message on the timing monitors. At this point the slower driver must let the faster driver overtake at the first opportunity. The rule requires this under the International Sporting Code (ISC), which says drivers who are caught by another car must allow the faster driver past.

Practice starts are allowed in special painted grid boxes during free practice sessions and during reconnaissance laps before the race. During free practice, practice starts may be performed in the merging lane to the right-hand side of the fast lane. During reconnaissance laps, cars wishing to do a practice start must use the pit exit road and may stop in the area before Safety Car Line 2. They must then rejoin from the pit exit road. Practice starts are not allowed during the qualifying session.

If qualifying is interrupted with less than 75 seconds remaining in any period, that period will not be resumed.

The Safety Car will not be signalled by waved yellow flags or "SC" boards. Instead, when the Safety Car is deployed, the message "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" will be sent to all teams and all trackside light panels will display "SC". When the Safety Car lights are turned off, the message "SAFETY CAR LIGHTS OFF" will be sent to all teams, and a green light panel will show at the control line.

The document also sets out rules for pit entry and pit exit, parc fermé access, removal of cars from the grid, track limits at specific turns, and changes made to the circuit for this event.

key_facts: This document sets out competition rules for the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix (13-15 March 2026).
It covers safety procedures, pit lane conduct, grid procedures, qualifying and practice practices, and circuit modifications at Shanghai.
The rules address drivers' obligations during lapping, starting procedures, and pit lane personnel restrictions to ensure safe and orderly racing.
summary.plain_explanation:
The FIA Race Director has issued competition notes for the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix. These notes give detailed instructions to teams and drivers about how to conduct themselves during the event.

On track, drivers must not exceed a maximum time between two safety car lines during Sprint Qualifying, Qualifying, and reconnaissance laps, or they may be deemed to be going unnecessarily slowly. During the Sprint and Race, drivers who are being lapped must allow faster drivers past at the first available opportunity when blue light panels are shown to them. Drivers must also avoid erratic acceleration, braking or manoeuvres after the safety car's orange lights are extinguished and before it returns to the pits.

In the pit lane, team personnel are only allowed there immediately before they need to work on a car, and must leave as soon as work is complete. After all cars able to do so have finished the Race, a message will be sent allowing pass holders who are not normally permitted in the pit lane to enter. Pit lane safety rules also apply until that point.

Practice starts during Free Practice can only be done on the grid, not at pit exit. During reconnaissance laps, cars wishing to do a practice start must use a specific part of the pit exit road and not cross a white line, and must keep to the right to let other cars pass.

On the grid, cars must be in a single line in the fast lane (the lane closest to the pit boxes) in the order they arrived there before a session starts. Drivers can blend into the fast lane from the inner lane if there is a suitable gap and they do this safely.

The notes also describe where certain equipment is placed around the circuit, how cars should be removed from the grid if needed, what happens if the race is suspended, and technical requirements such as ERS safety checks and driver weighing procedures.

summary.plain_explanation:
This document is the Race Director's Competition Notes for the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix and contains detailed instructions for running the event safely.

The document sets rules about pit lane safety and access. Team personnel are only allowed in the pit lane when they are about to work on a car or are working on it, and must leave as soon as work is done. After the race ends and all cars able to finish have reached the parc fermé area (the controlled parking area), the Race Director will send a message allowing anyone with a valid pass to enter the pit lane. The document reminds teams that they are responsible for all their employees, mechanics and other staff and their actions in the reserved areas.

On track, drivers must not go unnecessarily slowly. The maximum time from one safety car line to another on any lap during and after Sprint Qualifying and Qualifying, including practice laps, will be told to teams after practice. Drivers who are lapped during the Sprint and Race must let the faster car pass at the first safe chance. The car being lapped will receive blue light warnings when the faster car is close. When the safety car's orange lights go out and it is about to return to the pits, drivers must not accelerate or brake suddenly or do anything else that could endanger other drivers.

The document sets out detailed procedures for practice starts, which may only be done on the grid during practice sessions and during reconnaissance laps before the Sprint and Race, not at pit exit. During reconnaissance laps, cars wanting to do a practice start must use the pit exit road and stop at a marked white line, then rejoin the circuit from the pit exit road. Cars not doing a practice start must join the normal racing line at the first chance and not go back into the pit exit road.

Drivers entering the pit lane must stay to the right of a solid white line and may cross a dotted white line on the left, but cannot overtake in that area. The white line across pit exit marks the edge of the track. Team personnel are not allowed in the pit lane beyond the finish line during any live session.

Cars in the fast lane must form a line and leave in the order they arrived. Drivers may blend into the fast lane if there is a safe gap, but drivers in the inner lane parallel to the fast lane are not considered to have blended in at the earliest opportunity. Cars may not overtake others in the fast lane except in exceptional circumstances, such as when a car has a mechanical problem.

After qualifying sessions, drivers must go directly to the FIA scales to be weighed. Drivers finishing in the top 10 must go to the scales immediately when they leave their cars and may not contact anyone else first.

The parc fermé cameras must always be uncovered and working during the competition. Each morning after car covers are removed, all teams must connect telemetry equipment to their cars to check the ERS (energy recovery system) safety status. If a car's ERS is in hazard status, mechanics must report to race control after the session.

The document notes specific changes made to the circuit: the back of the kerb at the apex of Turn 3 has been lowered; the tyre barrier at Turn 7 on the left has been repositioned; and TSP 17, a timing sector point, has been moved 100 metres before Turn 14.

Practice starts are not allowed at pit exit but are permitted on the grid during free practice and on the pit exit road during reconnaissance laps.

summary.plain_explanation:
These are procedural instructions for the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix at Shanghai International Circuit, issued on 12 March 2026. The notes cover the rules teams and drivers must follow to ensure the competition runs safely and in order.

Drivers who are caught by a faster car must allow that car past at the first available opportunity. The marshalling system will give a warning when a faster car is within 3.0 seconds, and blue light panels will be shown when the faster car is within 1.2 seconds. When a safety car (a vehicle brought onto the track to slow drivers down and bunch them up during hazardous conditions) is returning to the pits after an orange lights (an instruction from the safety car to drivers to prepare for restart) are turned off, drivers must proceed without erratic acceleration, braking, or other manoeuvres that could endanger others.

During qualifying sessions and practice, drivers may not exceed a maximum time from the Second Safety Car Line to the First Safety Car Line on any lap. This applies to out-laps and in-laps (laps leaving and returning to the garage). If a driver exceeds this time, they may be penalised for going unnecessarily slowly. The maximum time will be told to teams and drivers after the practice session.

In the pit lane, team personnel are only allowed immediately before they are needed to work on a car and must leave as soon as work is complete. For the race only, this rule applies until all cars that can do so have finished and entered the parc fermé (a sealed area where cars are held under observation). After the race ends and the Race Director says it is safe, a message will tell pass holders they may access the pit lane.

Practice starts (standing starts practised before the race) may not be done at pit exit. They are allowed on the grid after free practice and on the pit exit road during reconnaissance laps (exploratory laps before the race), but not during qualifying. When practice starts happen on the pit exit road, cars wanting to do a practice start must stay left and stop at the white line; cars not doing one must cross to the track at the earliest chance.

Before each session starts, cars may not enter the pit lane to go to pit exit until 5 minutes before the session begins. If a session is stopped and restarted, cars may only enter the fast lane (the lane closer to the racing surface) after the restart time is confirmed by official messaging.

Drivers finishing in the top 10 must be weighed immediately after they leave their cars and before touching anyone. Other drivers who finish must go to the scales straight away after returning to their garage. Drivers may not drink or do anything that increases their weight before being weighed.

The circuit has three changes for this event. The back of the kerb (the edge of the track) at the apex of Turn 3 has been made lower. The tyre barrier at Turn 7 on the left side has been moved to a new position. Safety pole TSP 17, which sits before Turn 14, has been moved 100 metres further back.
